chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Nahdi, from Ibn Abi Anjarah, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever buys stolen goods while he knows, he has participated in its shame and its sin.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying stolen goods if you know they are stolen?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting that conscious purchase of stolen goods constitutes a form of partnership in the crime's moral and spiritual consequences, not just legal liability. This emphasizes the concept of 'sharing in the disgrace' (sharik fi 'arihi), linking the buyer's intent to the thief's act, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for determining the validity of transactions and distribution of khums or restitution.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Al Nahdy, from Ibn Abu Najran, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who buys stolen (goods) and he knows, so he has participated in its shame and in its sin’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-Nahdiy from ibn abu Najran from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whoever buys stolen goods when he knows it, he shares its shame and sin.’”
